title: fix(desktop): drag-out never copies the file and never deletes a drag in progress (audit LIB-B12)
body:
## What changed and why

This fixes audit finding **LIB-B12** (library lens B). Before this PR, dragging a titled recording out of Kaipu created a hard link in `<os-temp>/kaipu-drag/`. That caused two problems:

1. **Cross-volume copy.** When the vault is on another volume (an external disk or a custom folder), the temp dir is on a different device. `link()` then fails with `EXDEV`, and the whole video was **copied** before the drag could start.
2. **A second drag deleted the first.** Every drag wiped the entire `kaipu-drag` folder. A drop target still reading the first file (a Finder copy or an upload) could lose it mid-read.

The new behavior follows the approved spec `specs/2026-10-28-niw2-398-drag-out-volumes.md`:

- The per-drag folder is now `<vault>/.kaipu/drag/<uuid>/`. It is always on the vault's own volume, so the titled file is a hard link (no bytes copied) on APFS, NTFS and ext4.
- On `EXDEV` (a mount point inside the vault), the vault file itself is dragged under its id name. Nothing is copied and no folder is left behind.
- Any other link failure (exFAT and FAT have no hard links) falls back to `copyFile`, which keeps the title at the cost of a copy. If that copy fails with `ENOSPC`, the drag still fails with a logged error.
- If `mkdir` fails (read-only vault), the vault file itself is dragged.
- Each drag prunes only drag folders older than `DRAG_COPY_MAX_AGE_MS` (60 min), instead of wiping everything.
- Startup and quit wipe the current vault's `.kaipu/drag`. Startup also removes the legacy `<temp>/kaipu-drag` left by older builds.
- `drag-copies.ts` no longer imports `electron`. It takes the vault dir as an argument, and its tests use real temp dirs.

**Trade-off (the spec asks for it here):** on exFAT we copy the file to keep the title. The one-line alternative is to return `vaultFile` for every link error: it never copies, but on exFAT the dragged file is then named by id.

**Known limitation (accepted in the spec):** if the user changes the vault folder, the old vault's `.kaipu/drag` is no longer pruned. Hard links take no space.

`.kaipu/drag/` never shows up in the library. `LibraryVault.list()` reads the vault non-recursively and filters by media extension, and the other `.kaipu` readers only list their own `<id>.assets` folders.

This PR also deletes the plan file `plans/audit-2026-10-15/18-drag-out-volumes.md` and its row in `00-index.md`.

## How I verified it

- `bun run test src/main/library/drag-copies.test.ts` (from `apps/kaipu-record`) failed 9/9 before the rewrite and passes 9/9 after. The tests cover the five Review Focus points:
  - the dragged file has the same inode and `nlink === 2` under `.kaipu/drag`
  - `EXDEV` returns the vault file without copying
  - a second drag keeps the first file
  - pruning goes by age
  - cleanup leaves sidecars alone
- I ran `bun run verify` twice. The workflows check, lint, `oxfmt --check`, build and `check-types` all pass.
- In the tests, 2882 passed and **5 failed in both runs**. They are in `library-service.test.ts`, `recording-writer.test.ts` and `screenshots/export/export.test.ts`. None of those files touch drag code, and **the same 5 fail on the base commit `5af11515`** without this change. The cause: this Mac mini has no `node`, so vitest runs under Bun's Node shim. CI runs real Node and is the gate for those tests.
- Not run: the Playwright desktop E2E suite (CI runs it) and a manual drag in the real app.

## How to test it yourself

1. Export an MP4, then drag the status-card thumbnail into Finder. The file carries the title, and `ls -li "<vault>/.kaipu/drag/"*/` shows the same inode as `<vault>/<id>.mp4`.
2. Drag twice quickly. The first dropped file is still there.
3. Put the vault on an exFAT USB stick. The drag still works (a copy is made).
4. Quit. `<vault>/.kaipu/drag` is gone. A `$TMPDIR/kaipu-drag` left by an older build is gone after the next launch.

Refs NIW2-398
